LOW.rationale: Dormant/moored vessel or a device reporting once per hour (720 reports/month) with heartbeat. Payload ~0.3 KB plus MQTT/TLS overhead gives ~1.5 MB/month of billable cellular data; 5 MB retained locally in the cloud; one user alert per month, 10% of alerts escalated to SMS.

BASE.rationale: Coastal-cruising vessel reporting every 10 minutes (4,320 reports/month), including position, battery and one sensor set. 10 MB/month covers payload plus protocol overhead with headroom for firmware metadata; 20 MB retained per device in the cloud; six user alerts per device-month, 15% sent by SMS because push/email may be missed.

HIGH.rationale: Active passage with NMEA/engine telemetry every 2.5 minutes (17,520 reports/month) and richer payloads. 60 MB/month allows larger batches and occasional diagnostics uploads; 80 MB retained per device; 20 alerts/device-month with 20% via SMS. This is a modelling envelope, not a measured fleet profile.

fxBasis.sourceTitle: ECB euro reference exchange rates, 2 November 2026 (USD 1.1216 per EUR)
fxBasis.calculation: 1 / 1.1216 = 0.8915834, rounded to 0.8916 EUR per USD. All USD-converted inputs below use this rate.

inputs.item: Cellular IoT data, pay-as-you-go, Spain/EU zone - LOW profile
inputs.sourceTitle: Precios y planes de SIM IoT (iot.cards, retrieved 2026-11-02)
inputs.calculation: 1.5 MB/device-month x EUR 0.005/MB = EUR 0.007500/device-month (LOW data profile; no monthly minimum per SIM on the published pay-as-you-go tariff).
inputs.notes: Multi-operator Spain/EU SIM, no permanence. Tariff excludes VAT. This is a delivery-cost model, not a coverage or quality guarantee.

inputs.item: Cellular IoT data, pay-as-you-go, Spain/EU zone - BASE profile
inputs.sourceTitle: Precios y planes de SIM IoT (iot.cards, retrieved 2026-11-02)
inputs.calculation: 10 MB/device-month x EUR 0.005/MB = EUR 0.050000/device-month (BASE data profile; no monthly minimum per SIM).
inputs.notes: Lowest published Spain/EU rate captured. SIM hardware and activation are not included because no activation fee is published; a one-time SIM cost would be added if the SIM were not already part of hardware.

inputs.item: Cellular IoT data, pay-as-you-go, Spain/EU zone - HIGH profile
inputs.sourceTitle: Precios y planes de SIM IoT (iot.cards, retrieved 2026-11-02)
inputs.calculation: 60 MB/device-month x EUR 0.005/MB = EUR 0.300000/device-month (HIGH data profile).
inputs.notes: No volume discount is published for this rate; per-zone rates outside Spain/EU differ and were not captured.

inputs.item: 1NCE IoT Lifetime Flat - EUR 12 one-time for 10 years (500 MB total)
inputs.sourceTitle: Planes y precios de la SIM IoT 1NCE (retrieved 2026-11-02)
inputs.calculation: EUR 12.00 / 120 months = EUR 0.100000/device-month if consumption stays within 500 MB in 10 years (4.17 MB/month average). For the 10 MB/month BASE profile: 120 months x 10 MB = 1,200 MB, so (12 + 2 x 10) / 120 = EUR 32 / 120 = EUR 0.266667/device-month. For 60 MB/month HIGH the plan is not viable (7,200 MB needs 13 top-ups: (12 + 13 x 10) / 120 = EUR 1.183333/device-month).
inputs.notes: 1NCE is the cheapest published flat rate per device-year but the 500 MB cap over 10 years makes it suitable only for LOW telemetry. Includes 250 SMS (device-to-server only) and max 1 Mbit/s. Tariff is not a production entitlement.

inputs.item: planX3_EU 25 MB/month tier - first 12 months upfront
inputs.unit: EUR per device-month (first 12 months, committed upfront)
inputs.sourceTitle: European High Data IoT Pricing - planX3_EU (retrieved 2026-11-02)
inputs.calculation: EUR 4.50 upfront / 12 months = EUR 0.375000/device-month in year 1; from month 13 the published price is EUR 0.32/month; overage EUR 0.01/MB. 25 MB allowance covers the BASE 10 MB profile.
inputs.notes: Committed first-year cost is stepped: EUR 4.50 is payable before service starts. Prices exclude VAT. Alternative for a managed multi-country EU fleet; not a production entitlement.

inputs.item: AWS IoT Core telemetry ingestion - LOW profile
inputs.calculation: 720 messages/device-month = 0.000720 million messages x USD 1.00/million = USD 0.000720; x 0.8916 EUR/USD = EUR 0.000642/device-month. Connection charge is a separate input (RC-009).
inputs.notes: First 1B messages tier. Messages metered in 5 KB increments, so a larger payload costs more; LOW calculates one metered message per report.

inputs.item: AWS IoT Core telemetry ingestion - BASE profile
inputs.calculation: 4,320 messages/device-month = 0.004320 million x USD 1.00/million = USD 0.004320 x 0.8916 = EUR 0.003851/device-month.
inputs.notes: Assumes each telemetry report fits one 5 KB metered message. Rule-engine actions are not included (AWS prices them separately at USD 0.15/million actions).

inputs.item: AWS IoT Core telemetry ingestion - HIGH profile
inputs.calculation: 17,520 messages/device-month = 0.017520 million x USD 1.00/million = USD 0.017520 x 0.8916 = EUR 0.015621/device-month.
inputs.notes: No published volume discount before 1B messages/month; a 1,000-device HIGH fleet sends 17.5M messages/month, still inside the first tier.

inputs.item: AWS IoT Core device connection time - all profiles (8 h/day connected)
inputs.calculation: 8 h/day x 60 x 30 days = 14,400 connection-minutes/device-month = 0.014400 million x USD 0.08/million = USD 0.001152 x 0.8916 = EUR 0.001027/device-month. Always-on (24 h) would cost 3x: EUR 0.003081/device-month.
inputs.notes: Connection is metered per minute of authenticated MQTT/HTTP connection; 8 h/day is an engineering assumption for a periodically connected vessel device, not a measured figure.

inputs.item: Cloud compute + managed DB + object storage + egress - LOW profile
inputs.sourceTitle: Cloudflare R2 pricing + AWS Lambda pricing (retrieved 2026-11-02)
inputs.calculation: Lambda: 720 events x 0.5 GB x 0.2 s = 72 GB-s x USD 0.0000166667 = USD 0.001200; requests 0.000720M x USD 0.20 = USD 0.000144. R2: 720 Class A writes = 0.000720M x USD 4.50 = USD 0.003240; storage 0.005 GB x USD 0.015 = USD 0.000075; egress USD 0. Total USD 0.004659 x 0.8916 = EUR 0.004154/device-month.
inputs.notes: Managed database is DynamoDB at an unpublished-in-session price (RC-025), so DB cost is excluded, making this a floor. Egress is zero on R2. Class A writes dominate; batching reports would reduce this item materially.

inputs.item: Cloud compute + managed DB + object storage + egress - BASE profile
inputs.sourceTitle: Cloudflare R2 pricing + AWS Lambda pricing (retrieved 2026-11-02)
inputs.calculation: Lambda: 4,320 events x 0.5 GB x 0.2 s = 432 GB-s x USD 0.0000166667 = USD 0.007200; requests 0.004320M x USD 0.20 = USD 0.000864. R2: 4,320 Class A writes = 0.004320M x USD 4.50 = USD 0.019440; storage 0.020 GB x USD 0.015 = USD 0.000300; egress USD 0. Total USD 0.027804 x 0.8916 = EUR 0.024790/device-month.
inputs.notes: DB and monitoring are excluded (unpriced in session), so this is a floor, not a complete cloud cost. The R2 Class A write charge is the largest element; a 10-message batch would cut it ~10x and should be a design target.

inputs.item: Cloud compute + managed DB + object storage + egress - HIGH profile
inputs.sourceTitle: Cloudflare R2 pricing + AWS Lambda pricing (retrieved 2026-11-02)
inputs.calculation: Lambda: 17,520 events x 0.5 GB x 0.2 s = 1,752 GB-s x USD 0.0000166667 = USD 0.029200; requests 0.017520M x USD 0.20 = USD 0.003504. R2: 17,520 Class A writes = 0.017520M x USD 4.50 = USD 0.078840; storage 0.080 GB x USD 0.015 = USD 0.001200; egress USD 0. Total USD 0.112744 x 0.8916 = EUR 0.100526/device-month.
inputs.notes: Unbatched per-message writes; batching is the main cost lever. DB and monitoring remain excluded.

inputs.item: Azure IoT Hub S1 per device-month at 1 device (fixed unit floor)
inputs.unit: EUR per device-month (one S1 unit spread over 1 device)
inputs.calculation: S1 USD 25/unit-month x 0.8916 = EUR 22.290000/month for 1 S1 unit; at 1 active device = EUR 22.290000/device-month. S1 includes 400,000 messages/day = 12,000,000 messages/month, so one unit covers 1-1,000 devices at BASE (4,320 msgs/device-month x 1,000 = 4.32M < 12M) but only ~684 devices at HIGH (17,520 x 684 = 11.98M).
inputs.notes: Stepped fixed platform cost: per-device cost collapses with fleet size. Expensive for a 1-device pilot; compare with AWS pay-per-message below ~700 BASE devices.

inputs.item: Azure IoT Hub S1 per device-month at 10 devices
inputs.unit: EUR per device-month (one S1 unit spread over 10 devices)
inputs.calculation: EUR 22.290000/month / 10 devices = EUR 2.229000/device-month.
inputs.notes: Still one S1 unit; no additional tier needed at BASE or LOW intensity.

inputs.item: Azure IoT Hub S1 per device-month at 100 devices
inputs.unit: EUR per device-month (one S1 unit spread over 100 devices)
inputs.calculation: EUR 22.290000/month / 100 devices = EUR 0.222900/device-month.
inputs.notes: One S1 unit still covers 100 devices at BASE.

inputs.item: Azure IoT Hub S1 per device-month at 500 and 1,000 devices
inputs.unit: EUR per device-month (one S1 unit spread over 1,000 devices)
inputs.calculation: 500 devices: EUR 22.290000 / 500 = EUR 0.044580/device-month. 1,000 devices: EUR 22.290000 / 1,000 = EUR 0.022290/device-month. HIGH at 1,000 devices: 17.52M messages/month > 12M included, so 2 S1 units = EUR 44.580000/month = EUR 0.044580/device-month (message overage pricing not captured).
inputs.notes: Stepped behaviour with a capacity cliff at ~684 HIGH devices/unit. Values per unit are published; the fleet division is explicit arithmetic.

inputs.item: Workers Paid plan floor, amortised at 1,000 devices
inputs.calculation: USD 5.00/month x 0.8916 = EUR 4.458000/organization-month. Per device-month at 1,000 active devices: 4.458000 / 1,000 = EUR 0.004458; at 1 device = EUR 4.458000. Annual floor: 4.458000 x 12 = EUR 53.496000/year.
inputs.notes: Fixed account floor for API/auth/tenant-isolation functions and scheduled jobs. Free tier exists but is NOT a production entitlement.

inputs.item: Push notification delivery to mobile/web clients
inputs.unit: EUR per push notification (published no-cost service)
inputs.calculation: 0 EUR x any alert volume = EUR 0.000000 per push notification; alerts routed to push are costed at zero in the model.
inputs.notes: No-cost is not a delivery guarantee: FCM delivery is best-effort, so the model must never be restated as a guaranteed alert-delivery promise. A paid push provider (e.g. OneSignal) was not priced in this session.

inputs.item: Amazon SES transactional email (per 1,000 emails and per email)
inputs.calculation: USD 0.11 per 1,000 emails x 0.8916 = EUR 0.098076 per 1,000; per email = 0.098076 / 1,000 = EUR 0.000098076. BASE alert email share: 6 alerts x 85% email = 5.1 emails/device-month x 0.000098076 = EUR 0.000500/device-month.
inputs.notes: USD 0.11 is the lowest of the nine per-1,000 prices visible on the page; the plan/volume mapping was not unambiguous, so this is a floor requiring confirmation.

inputs.item: Outbound SMS to Spain (alert escalation)
inputs.sourceTitle: SMS Pricing in Spain for Text Messaging (retrieved 2026-11-02)
inputs.calculation: USD 0.0875 per outbound SMS to Spain x 0.8916 = EUR 0.078015 per SMS. Carrier fees, sender-ID registration and shortcode fees are excluded.
inputs.notes: Highest per-alert channel cost in the model; SMS share drives alert cost. Price is a published list rate, not a negotiated or guaranteed rate.

inputs.provider: Firebase Cloud Messaging + Amazon SES + Twilio
inputs.item: Alert delivery cost (push + email + SMS mix) - LOW profile
inputs.calculation: 1 alert x (10% SMS x EUR 0.078015 + 90% email x EUR 0.000098076) = 0.0078015 + 0.0000883 = EUR 0.0078898/device-month; push is EUR 0.
inputs.notes: Modelled delivery cost only; never a guaranteed alert-delivery claim.

inputs.provider: Firebase Cloud Messaging + Amazon SES + Twilio
inputs.item: Alert delivery cost (push + email + SMS mix) - BASE profile
inputs.calculation: 6 alerts x (15% SMS x EUR 0.078015 + 85% email x EUR 0.000098076) = 6 x (0.0117023 + 0.0000834) = EUR 0.0707137/device-month; push is EUR 0.
inputs.notes: SMS escalation is ~99% of the alert cost. Reducing SMS share or using in-app/push fallbacks is the main lever.

inputs.provider: Firebase Cloud Messaging + Amazon SES + Twilio
inputs.item: Alert delivery cost (push + email + SMS mix) - HIGH profile
inputs.calculation: 20 alerts x (20% SMS x EUR 0.078015 + 80% email x EUR 0.000098076) = 20 x (0.0156030 + 0.0000785) = EUR 0.3136292/device-month; push is EUR 0.
inputs.notes: HIGH alert volume plus 20% SMS more than triples alert cost versus BASE. Alert volume must be demand-validated before it is treated as a product assumption.

inputs.item: Card payment fee - 1.5% + EUR 0.25 (standard EEA cards)
inputs.unit: EUR fixed fee per transaction plus 1.5% of transaction value
inputs.calculation: Fee = 1.5% x transaction value + EUR 0.25. For a EUR 10.00 monthly subscription: 0.015 x 10 + 0.25 = EUR 0.40 per transaction (4.00% of revenue); for EUR 120.00 annual: 1.80 + 0.25 = EUR 2.05 (1.71% of revenue). UK cards 2.5% + 0.25; international cards 2.8% + 0.25.
inputs.notes: Revenue-side deduction, NOT a cost of goods; never subtracted from COGS. Card data is never stored by MAREA (hosted/tokenised flows only).

inputs.item: Chargeback / dispute fee
inputs.sourceTitle: Stripe Spain pricing - Disputes section present but amount not captured (retrieved 2026-11-02)
inputs.calculation: NOT COMPUTED: the Stripe pricing page contains dispute received/countered/appealed fee rows, but the retrieved static text did not expose an unambiguous amount-to-row mapping. Value intentionally null rather than guessed.
inputs.notes: Gap. A per-dispute fee plus the disputed amount (and possible refund) must be obtained from Stripe's published fee schedule before chargeback cost can be modelled.

inputs.item: Stripe Billing (recurring subscription add-on)
inputs.sourceTitle: Stripe Spain pricing - Billing section present, rate not captured (retrieved 2026-11-02)
inputs.calculation: NOT COMPUTED: the Billing percentage was not present in the retrieved static text. Model currently charges only the Payments fee (RC-024).
inputs.notes: Gap; if Stripe Billing is adopted, its percentage must be added on top of the card fee.

inputs.item: App Store commission - Small Business Program 15%
inputs.unit: EUR deducted per EUR 10.00 App Store transaction (15% commission)
inputs.calculation: 15% x EUR 10.00 = EUR 1.50 deducted per EUR 10.00 transaction (EUR 8.50 net before tax). Applies only if prior-year proceeds are <= USD 1,000,000 and the developer is accepted into the program.
inputs.notes: Revenue-side deduction, not a cost of goods. The non-qualifying 30% standard commission was not explicitly evidenced on the retrieved page; if the program is not granted, the deduction doubles and that case must be modelled separately.

inputs.item: Google Play service fee - 15% tier
inputs.unit: EUR deducted per EUR 10.00 Play transaction (15% service fee tier)
inputs.calculation: 15% x EUR 10.00 = EUR 1.50 deducted per EUR 10.00 transaction (EUR 8.50 net before tax). Google states 99% of fee-paying developers are eligible for 15% or less; the 30% tier applies to other transactions under the new/existing install rules and was not numerically evidenced in this session.
inputs.notes: Revenue-side deduction, not a cost of goods. The 30% case must be priced before any Play revenue model is treated as complete.

inputs.item: Managed database (DynamoDB) and monitoring (CloudWatch) per device-month
inputs.sourceTitle: AWS pricing pages are client-side rendered; S3 storage, DynamoDB and CloudWatch rates not retrievable (retrieved 2026-11-02)
inputs.calculation: NOT COMPUTED: AWS S3 storage, DynamoDB and CloudWatch price tables are JavaScript-rendered and the served HTML contains no numeric rate; the bulk price-list endpoint returned 404. No value is guessed.
inputs.notes: Material gap: RC-011/RC-012 exclude managed DB and monitoring, so cloud cost is a floor. Cloudflare R2 substitutes only for object storage.

inputs.item: Fixed annual monitoring/backup minimum
inputs.sourceTitle: No retrievable published CloudWatch/AWS Backup rate in session (retrieved 2026-11-02)
inputs.calculation: NOT COMPUTED: no CloudWatch or AWS Backup price could be retrieved. The known fixed floor in the model is instead the Cloudflare Workers Paid minimum (EUR 53.496/year, RC-017).
inputs.notes: Gap. A production monitoring/backup floor must be quoted before any cost-per-device figure is presented as complete.

inputs.item: EU data-residency region uplift
inputs.sourceTitle: EU region (Europe West/North) was the region used for all captured cloud prices
inputs.calculation: Assumed EUR 0.000000 uplift because all cloud prices captured in MC-12 already use EU regions (AWS eu-west-1/Ireland example, Azure Europe West/North). No separate EU-residency surcharge was found in the retrieved sources.
inputs.notes: Data-residency note: Azure/AWS/Cloudflare EU regions are the modelling basis; DynamoDB/CloudWatch and Hetzner remain unpriced, and no contractually guaranteed data-residency commitment exists. GDPR transfer analysis belongs to the legal workstream.

inputs.item: Tenant isolation at application layer (Workers per-tenant execution)
inputs.calculation: Assumed EUR 0.000000 because tenant isolation is implemented with Workers routing/namespace checks inside the Workers Paid floor (RC-017); no per-tenant isolation line item is published. AWS Lambda tenant-isolation charges exist as a capability but no rate was retrieved.
inputs.notes: Engineering assumption only. If per-tenant execution environments (Lambda tenant isolation) are adopted, this assumption becomes a real cost.

inputs.item: Object storage egress (data transfer out)
inputs.calculation: 0 x any GB volume = EUR 0.000000; R2 egress is published as free for Standard and Infrequent Access.
inputs.notes: Zero egress is specific to R2; AWS S3 egress rates were not retrieved and would differ.

inputs.item: Support incident handling cost
inputs.unit: EUR per support incident (internal engineering estimate)
inputs.sourceTitle: No support cost is published by any provider; internal engineering estimate (retrieved 2026-11-02)
inputs.calculation: Assumed 0.5 h of engineering time x EUR 30/h = EUR 15.00 per incident. BASE: 1 incident/100 devices-month x EUR 15 = EUR 0.15/device-month; LOW: 0.2/100 x 15 = EUR 0.03/device-month; HIGH: 2/100 x 15 = EUR 0.30/device-month.
inputs.notes: Pure engineering assumption with no published evidence; sensitivity is high and it is not part of the connectivity/cloud vendor cost.

inputs.item: Offshore / blue-water connectivity
inputs.sourceTitle: Engineering assumption; terrestrial coverage pages do not state offshore coverage
inputs.calculation: NOT COMPUTED: terrestrial cellular coverage is not assumed offshore. All cellular inputs RC-001..RC-005 apply only inside terrestrial coverage; satellite connectivity is out of scope and has no price in this file.
inputs.notes: Explicit modelling boundary. No claim of offshore connectivity or alert delivery is made anywhere in MC-12.
